leads.summary: Live EasyEffects routing to Bluetooth or other non-ALSA output is ignored
leads.consequence: With default easyeffects_sink and an active ee_soe_output_level link to bluez_output.*, raop_output.* or another non-ALSA sink, the branch ignores the real endpoint. With no readable EE config it returns easyeffects_sink; with a persisted, available but now outdated ALSA outputDevice it can select that unrelated device instead. Volume keys, the audio panel and switch OSD then read/change the wrong sink. Synthetic Bluetooth link run emitted easyeffects_sink, versus expected bluez_output. This also applies when the open AirPlay PR #9221 supplies raop_output sinks.

leads.summary: Idle fallback mistakes an autosaved snapshot for EasyEffects' current output selection
leads.consequence: EasyEffects changes outputDevice in memory when its output selection changes (or when it follows a changed system default), but persists it on a 30-second autosave, or on hiding/exiting the UI. During idle (or between relinking), if both old and new ALSA sinks remain available, the stale file passes existence validation and the resolver directs the volume controls and bar to the old device. With the UI closed the autosave timer is stopped and this can persist until the next save. Synthetic two-ALSA-sink reproduction returns the old name; this models the upstream documented update/save ordering, not a hardware observation.
leads.triage: stale autosave; matches Opus finding 1 source evidence; folded into finding 1 text

leads.summary: Idle fallback never reads EasyEffects Flatpak settings
leads.consequence: Flatpak saves the same KConfig entry under the per-app host config directory (~/.var/app/com.github.wwmm.easyeffects/config/easyeffects/db/easyeffectsrc), rather than the host XDG_CONFIG_HOME. When EasyEffects has no live port links, the resolver cannot find that configured output and returns easyeffects_sink. The keys and panel then change the virtual sink's volume rather than the configured output. Synthetic reproduction emits easyeffects_sink with a valid per-app key and a present output sink.
leads.triage: Flatpak path; = Opus note 3; mentioned as example in finding 1

leads.summary: Configured sink existence test uses regex rather than literal sink name
leads.consequence: grep -qx treats the dots in a normal ALSA node name as wildcards. A stale configured name can match a different still-existing sink, so the resolver prints a sink which does not exist at all. The volume caller then cannot read that sink's volume or change it; its numeric actions print an error, while switch falls back to its JSON level and mute defaults to false. A synthetic name differing by one character returned the nonexistent configured name. #8713's overlapping code uses grep -qxF for this check.
leads.triage: regex vs literal; = Opus note 2; optional note

leads.summary: Three diverged open PRs need manual reconciliation at this resolver, #9132 also adds the identical test path
leads.consequence: #9132 adds a traversal to the same location and independently introduces test/shell.d/audio-output-sink-test.sh, so a textual merge of these heads conflicts in both production and test files. #12299 replaces the resolver with general PipeWire discovery, and #8713 adds a nearly equivalent EE fallback; both produce conflicting resolver hunks. All three heads diverge from #13396, not stacked. If either merges first, #13396 cannot be integrated unmodified; decide which resolver and tests to retain. GitHub currently calls the other PRs MERGEABLE against their own base, which does not imply their combination merges. New #12842 and #12300 touch only the separate tuning detection function and do not create this textual conflict.
leads.triage: overlap #8713/#9132/#12299; = Opus note 6; verified #9132 adds same test file (intake/pr9132.diff)

leads.summary: New pw-link fixture does not validate the CLI option it purports to test
leads.consequence: The stub always emits port links regardless of pw-link's arguments. A plausible broken refactor invoking pw-link without -l (no link listing) or with -o rather than -l still makes the new playing test pass, while the real 1.6.8 tool does not provide those link lines. Require '$*' == '-l' in the stub and cover the missing-link behaviour. All five present cases pass at the reviewed head, so this is a low-priority test-fidelity gap rather than a demonstrated production regression.
leads.triage: pw-link stub ignores args; verified in diff line 24-27; dropped as low value (no demonstrated surviving mutant run)

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** While EasyEffects plays into Bluetooth headphones, the live port link is ignored and the resolver falls back to `easyeffectsrc`, or to `easyeffects_sink` when there is none.

### Only `alsa_output.*` links are followed

`bin/omarchy-audio-output-sink:64` skips `ee_soe_output_level:output_FL |-> bluez_output.…:playback_FL`, so the resolver falls back to the settings file. **Impact:** with no `easyeffectsrc` (for example a Flatpak install) the keys still move the inert `easyeffects_sink`; with a file naming another present device, they change that device's volume instead of the headphones'. EasyEffects 8.2.9 saves that file only when its window hides or closes, every 30 s by default while it is shown, and on quit, so in service mode it can be out of date.

**Suggested change:** Match any sink playback port (`$2 ~ /:playback_/`), and add a Bluetooth scenario to the test.

<details><summary>Reproducer</summary>

# Reproducer: live EasyEffects link to a Bluetooth sink is ignored

Synthetic, stub-based (no audio server). Append either block, unchanged, to the
end of `test/shell.d/audio-output-sink-test.sh` at the reviewed head
(91fd24c2b1bc86ea458f0f6a3bf0ac83ab46ef31) and run
`bash test/shell.d/audio-output-sink-test.sh`. The blocks reuse the file's own
`reset_scenario`, `resolve` and `$physical`.

## Block A: Bluetooth link, settings file still names the speakers

```bash
# EasyEffects playing into Bluetooth headphones: the live port links name the
# headphones, while the settings file still names the speakers (EasyEffects
# writes easyeffectsrc only when its window closes, on a 30 s autosave while the
# window is open, and on quit). The live link should win.
headphones=bluez_output.00_11_22_33_44_55.1
reset_scenario
printf '267\t%s\tPipeWire\ts32le 4ch 44100Hz\tSUSPENDED\n301\t%s\tPipeWire\ts16le 2ch 48000Hz\tRUNNING\n870\teasyeffects_sink\tPipeWire\tfloat32le 2ch 48000Hz\tRUNNING\n' \
  "$physical" "$headphones" >"$test_home/data/sinks"
cat >"$test_home/data/links" <<LINKS
ee_soe_output_level:output_FL
  |-> $headphones:playback_FL
ee_soe_output_level:output_FR
  |-> $headphones:playback_FR
LINKS
mkdir -p "$test_home/.config/easyeffects/db"
printf '[StreamOutputs]\noutputDevice=%s\n' "$physical" >"$test_home/.config/easyeffects/db/easyeffectsrc"
resolved=$(resolve)
printf '# bluetooth link + settings naming the speakers -> %s\n' "$resolved"
[[ $resolved == "$headphones" ]] ||
  fail "easyeffects_sink playing into Bluetooth resolves to the headphones" "expected: $headphones"$'\n'"actual:   $resolved"
pass "easyeffects_sink playing into Bluetooth resolves to the headphones"
```

Actual output at the reviewed head, exit status 1.

stdout:

```
ok - physical default sink resolves to itself
ok - easyeffects_sink resolves through its port links
ok - idle easyeffects_sink resolves through the configured output device
ok - missing configured device falls back to the DSP sink
ok - filter-chain tuning resolves through its stream
# bluetooth link + settings naming the speakers -> alsa_output.pci-0000_00_1f.3.analog-surround-40
```

stderr:

```

actual:   alsa_output.pci-0000_00_1f.3.analog-surround-40
not ok - easyeffects_sink playing into Bluetooth resolves to the headphones
```

## Block B: Bluetooth link, no settings file

```bash

# example a Flatpak install, whose settings live under ~/.var/app).
headphones=bluez_output.00_11_22_33_44_55.1

printf '267\t%s\tPipeWire\ts32le 4ch 44100Hz\tSUSPENDED\n301\t%s\tPipeWire\ts16le 2ch 48000Hz\tRUNNING\n870\teasyeffects_sink\tPipeWire\tfloat32le 2ch 48000Hz\tRUNNING\n' \
  "$physical" "$headphones" >"$test_home/data/sinks"
cat >"$test_home/data/links" <<LINKS
ee_soe_output_level:output_FL
  |-> $headphones:playback_FL
ee_soe_output_level:output_FR
  |-> $headphones:playback_FR
LINKS
resolved=$(resolve)
printf '# bluetooth link, no settings file -> %s\n' "$resolved"
[[ $resolved == "$headphones" ]] ||
  fail "easyeffects_sink playing into Bluetooth resolves to the headphones without a settings file" "expected: $headphones"$'\n'"actual:   $resolved"
pass "easyeffects_sink playing into Bluetooth resolves to the headphones without a settings file"
```

Actual output at the reviewed head, exit status 1.

```
ok - physical default sink resolves to itself
ok - easyeffects_sink resolves through its port links
ok - idle easyeffects_sink resolves through the configured output device
ok - missing configured device falls back to the DSP sink
ok - filter-chain tuning resolves through its stream

```

actual:   easyeffects_sink

## With the suggested change

In a disposable copy of the resolver, replacing `$2 ~ /^alsa_output\..*:playback_/`
with `$2 ~ /:playback_/` made the five existing scenarios, both blocks above and a
"live ALSA link beats a settings file naming another present card" scenario pass
(exit 0).

</details>

<details><summary>Optional notes</summary>

- **Test header:** `docs/testing.md` asks every shell test to start with `set -euo pipefail` and the `BASH_SOURCE` source line. Without it, a failed `mktemp -d` leaves `test_home` empty and `reset_scenario` runs `rm -rf "/data" "/.config"`; with the documented header it stops at the `mktemp` failure instead, and with a working `mktemp` all five scenarios still pass.
- **Literal match:** `grep -qxF "$configured"` compares the configured sink name literally instead of as a regex (`.` is a wildcard today).
- **Overlap:** #8713, #9132 and #12299 change the same resolver hunk (#9132 also adds `test/shell.d/audio-output-sink-test.sh`), and issues #9021 and #12204 describe this bug.

</details>

<details><summary>Reproducer: test header</summary>

# Reproducer: the new test keeps going after `mktemp -d` fails

The new `test/shell.d/audio-output-sink-test.sh` has no `set -euo pipefail`
(the header `docs/testing.md` prescribes for every shell test). When `mktemp -d`
fails, `test_home` and `test_bin` are empty and `reset_scenario` goes on to run
`rm -rf "/data" "/.config"` and `mkdir -p "/data"`.

Safe to run: `rm`, `mkdir`, `pactl` and `pw-link` are replaced by stubs that
only print what would have run. Run from the repository root at the reviewed
head (91fd24c2b1bc86ea458f0f6a3bf0ac83ab46ef31):

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Run from the repository root at the reviewed head. rm and mkdir (and the audio
# clients) are replaced by stubs that only print what would have run, so nothing
# is removed and no audio server is queried.
guard=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$guard"' EXIT
for tool in rm mkdir pactl pw-link; do
  cat >"$guard/$tool" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/bash
printf 'would run: %s %s\n' "$(basename "$0")" "$*" >&2
exit 1
STUB
  chmod +x "$guard/$tool"
done
TMPDIR=/nonexistent PATH="$guard:$PATH" bash test/shell.d/audio-output-sink-test.sh
echo "exit=$?"
```

Actual output (run in a sandbox whose root filesystem is read-only, hence
"Read-only file system" where a normal host would say "Permission denied").

stdout:

```
exit=1
```

stderr:

```
mktemp: failed to create directory via template ‘/nonexistent/tmp.XXXXXXXXXX’: No such file or directory
mktemp: failed to create directory via template ‘/nonexistent/tmp.XXXXXXXXXX’: No such file or directory
test/shell.d/audio-output-sink-test.sh: line 15: /pactl: Read-only file system
test/shell.d/audio-output-sink-test.sh: line 24: /pw-link: Read-only file system
chmod: cannot access '/pactl': No such file or directory
chmod: cannot access '/pw-link': No such file or directory
would run: rm -rf /data /.config
would run: mkdir -p /data
test/shell.d/audio-output-sink-test.sh: line 40: /data/default-sink: No such file or directory
test/shell.d/audio-output-sink-test.sh: line 41: /data/sinks: No such file or directory
test/shell.d/audio-output-sink-test.sh: line 47: /data/default-sink: No such file or directory
not ok - a physical default sink resolves to itself
would run: rm -rf  
```

With the documented header (`set -euo pipefail` and the `BASH_SOURCE` source
line) the same file stops at the first `mktemp -d` failure: its only output is the
first `mktemp: failed to create directory ...` line and no `rm` or `mkdir` call is
made. With that header and a working `mktemp`, all five of the PR's scenarios still
pass.

</details>
